title: reduce-proxy-headroom-and-enforce-route-payload-quota
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent streaming stalls and truncated structured outputs from the OpenAI-compat gateway under sustained concurrent streaming traffic, especially when requests included tool/function-calling and large JSON structured-output payloads. Root cause analysis pointed at oversized proxy buffer headroom plus lack of per-route payload quota enforcement which allowed some long-poll requests to exhaust upstream connection resources and cause head-of-line blocking. Changes: 1) Reduce default proxy write/read headroom from 1MB to 256KB and make it configurable per-route. 2) Introduce per-route payload byte quota and hard limit enforcement for sync (non-streaming) requests; requests over quota are rejected with 413 or 429 depending on route config and provide a Retry-After header. 3) Adjust streaming proxy chunk flush thresholds to favor more frequent smaller flushes for function/tool-calling streams so structured output arrives earlier and is less likely to be dropped. 4) Add a lightweight in-memory per-connection backpressure counter to deprioritize new large non-streaming requests when streaming sessions are active. 5) Extend OpenAI-compat layer to include a compatibility shim that maps oversized completion responses to a streaming fallback when route allows streaming, preserving function-call markers and structured JSON chunks. 6) Add metrics: gateway.proxy.buffer_headroom_bytes, gateway.route.payload_quota_exceeded, gateway.stream.flush_count and an alert to detect sustained per-route 413/429 spikes. Tests: added unit tests for headroom config parsing and quota logic, integration tests simulating concurrent streaming plus large sync requests, and a perf canary harness that validates stable p95 latency under 1000 concurrent streaming clients. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag gateway.buffering.v2 and staged canary at 5%->25%->100% with monitoring queries for errors and alloc spikes. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is conservative and non-breaking; routes that depend on previous large single-request semantics can opt out by setting route.payload_quota_bytes to 0. Related work: this complements ENG-1452 batching improvements and addresses customer escalations in SUP-883. See notes for follow-ups to expose finer-grained telemetry and an SDK handshake for early client backpressure negotiation.

release_notes: Gateway: reduce default proxy buffer headroom to improve streaming stability; add per-route payload byte quota with opt-out; streaming proxy now flushes smaller chunks for function/tool-calling to preserve structured output delivery. Rollout gated behind gateway.buffering.v2 and subject to canary. No breaking changes by default; routes can opt out.
testing: local unit/coverage for buffer_manager and payload_quota
integration harness simulating 1000 concurrent streaming clients + periodic 1MB sync requests
benchmarks validating p95 latency under canary
rollout: Canary rollout plan: enable gateway.buffering.v2 at 5% traffic for 24h, monitor gateway.route.payload_quota_exceeded and p95 latency, expand to 25% for 48h, then 100% if no regressions. Automated rollback if 5x baseline error rate or >30% p95 latency regression.
